name: hbt-kaband-characterization
description: Ka-band (17.7 / 19.45 / 21.2 GHz) device characterization of a bare npn13G2 HBT behind ideal bias tees: two-port noise parameters (NFmin, Zopt, Rn) from noiseless passive source impedances with the source noise added analytically at an explicit T0, NF into 50 ohm, fT from the h21 0 dB crossing, Rollett K / |Delta| and MAG-or-MSG, and DC power -- swept over Nx x VCE x VBE (measured J_C) inside every HBT process x temperature x supply point.
claim: DEVICE-LEVEL EVIDENCE, NOT A MATCHED-AMPLIFIER RESULT: every number is a two-port parameter of one bare npn13G2 with ideal bias tees and ideal noiseless source/load terminations. NFmin is a lower bound on what a circuit built around this device could reach before matching-network loss, bias-network noise and the following stage; MAG/MSG is device gain, not a designed stage's gain. Nothing here claims any spec/target-spec.md row is met; the row-3 comparison is a feasibility screen only.
netlist_provenance: schematic (device-characterization fixture: one bare npn13G2 per copy with ideal bias tees and ideal noiseless terminations; no design/ schematic exists and this is not one)
_harness_measure_note: The 'analyses'/'measure' pair above is ONLY what a bare `python3 -m harness.cli run|selftest hbt-kaband-characterization` evaluates: |h21| at 100 GHz at the fixture's default bias (Nx=4, VCE=1.0 V, VBE=0.88 V), a cheap process-sensitive scalar that keeps the generic harness path working for this bench. The characterization itself is the 'sweep' block below, driven by ../run.py (see ../README.md); sim/characterize.sh uses run.py, not harness.cli, for this bench.

_notes: nx: three declared emitter multiplicities inside the model card's 'Valid numbers: NX = 1 - 10'.

vce_v: the collector-emitter voltages the supply decision must choose from (issue #17 names 0.6/1.0/1.4 V). 1.4 V is BVCEO min (spec/target-spec.md row 17); all three sit inside the card's vce 0.4-2.0 V validity window.

vbe_v: the swept quantity; J_C is MEASURED (Ic from the op point / (Nx * 0.063 um^2)), not targeted. 0.60-1.04 V crosses BOTH ends of the card's vbe 0.65-0.96 V window on purpose (VBE for a given J_C moves by roughly -1.3 mV/K, so the window maps to very different J_C ranges at -40 and 125 C) so that the in-box optimum is either bracketed or shown to be constrained by a named bound at every temperature; every row carries validity_flags and out-of-box rows are excluded from the in-box (reported) optimum.

source_impedances_ohm: [R, X] pairs realised at each frequency by the fixture's noiseless rsz-lsz-csz chain. The first four MUST be R1, R2, R1+jX, R1-jX (the in-deck closed form that picks the independent optimum check point); all ten enter the least-squares noise-parameter fit. The set spans 25 ohm to 1000+1500j ohm because Zopt scales roughly as 1/Nx and reaches ~1300+1600j ohm at Nx=1; with a narrower closed-form set (25/100/25+-50j) the in-deck optimum extrapolated poorly for those devices (check point up to 0.003 dB above NFmin, vs ~1e-5 dB with this set).
nf50_check_ohm: the 50 ohm source used for NF_50 and as the independent check of the fit (deliberately not one of the fitted impedances).

t0_k: 290 K is the IEEE noise-figure reference (used for the row-3 screen); 300.15 K is the repo's porting-plan convention (spec/porting-plan.md section 1), reported alongside. Tmin (K) is T0-independent and is recorded too.
reduced: smoke/selftest bias axes only; every RF definition is inherited from full.

evidence.data_provenance: simulated (ngspice, real npn13G2 VBIC model from the installed IHP-Open-PDK cornerHBT.lib, ideal bias tees and ideal noiseless terminations; no PDK inductor model or matching network anywhere)
notes: Device-level evidence only; not a matched-amplifier result. See the testbench claim.

Source-noise reference: the source resistor is noisy=0 and its thermal noise is added analytically at an explicit T0 (F = 1 + Sv/(4 k T0 Re Zs)); the load is noisy=0 and excluded from the device figure. The per-instance resistor temp= convention is NOT used -- see README.md for the ngspice-46 resistor probe.
Supply axis: present in every deck as an unconnected ideal rail; the ideal regulated bias makes it physically inert by construction. No supply-sensitivity floor is attached.
